disclosurePolicy.whatIsRecorded: structural facts about the egress path, plus two IANA-operated public canaries that are not part of any draw
canariesUsed: ipv4only.arpa - the IETF well-known name whose AAAA answer is precisely how DNS64 announces itself

theConditionBeingRuledOut.name: IPV6_ONLY_CELLULAR_DNS64_NAT64_TRANSLATION_PREFIX_ONLY_VANTAGE
asObservedDuringWindow02: IPv6-only cellular uplink as the sole egress

defaultRoute.note: a private LAN IPv4 with ordinary public IPv4 egress is the normal and acceptable shape; the local interface does not need a public IPv4 address

dns64Probe.name: ipv4only.arpa
dns64Probe.why: under DNS64 this name's AAAA answer is synthesised into the operator's translation prefix. An EMPTY AAAA answer alongside the real A records is the direct negative

gatewayOwnResolverPathProbe.why: the strongest available proof is not curl's resolver but the EXACT call the landed gateway makes. src/orgunits/web/gateway.ts resolves with dnsPromises.lookup(hostname, { all: true, verbatim: true }); that same call was made here against the non-institution canaries
gatewayOwnResolverPathProbe.classifierUsed: the landed, unmodified classifyIpAddress from src/orgunits/web/address.ts

results.note: this name is SUPPOSED to be refused by the guard - 192.0.0.0/24 is an IETF protocol assignment. It is used here as a DNS64 detector, never as a connectivity canary

guardStillRefusesTranslationPrefixes.why: proving the vantage changed must not be confused with proving the guard was loosened. The same unmodified classifier that now accepts ordinary public IPv4 still refuses every address that caused the Window-02 refusals
